properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 27 at 9:00PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Persistent and gusty northeast winds are slowing river flow. The St
Johns River at Astor will remain in Moderate Flood Stage, though
river levels are forecast to slowly decline through this weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, Bonnet and Snail roads. Roads along Blue
Creek are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter,
Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Tuesday the stage was 3.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EDT Tuesday was 3.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 3.8 feet
just after midnight tonight.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday morning at 1100 AM EDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE

properties.areaDesc: Alamosa, CO; Conejos, CO; Costilla, CO; Rio Grande, CO
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 27 at 9:07PM MDT until October 27 at 10:45PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding continues, especially along and near the Rio Grande
and Conejos River.

* WHERE...Northeastern Conejos County, West Central Costilla County,
Southeastern Rio Grande County, and Southwestern Alamosa County...

* WHEN...Until 1045 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is occurring, especially in areas along
and near the Conejos River and the Rio Grande. Widespread
inundation of agriculture fields, wetlands, and other low-lying
areas persists. Areas of standing or slow moving water will
continue over many roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 906 PM MDT, Flooding was still occurring in the warning area,
especially in low-lying areas.
- Water levels continues to remain elevated within the Conejos
River near Manassa. In addition, Widespread inundation of
agriculture fields, wetlands, and other low-lying areas.
- Low lying areas in Conejos, Costilla, Rio Grande and Alamosa
counties are impacted, especially along and near the Rio Grande
and Conejos River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Heed all road closures and directives from law enforcement and local
emergency management.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL 1045 PM MDT THIS EVENING

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 27 at 6:50PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Rio Chama Below Chamita affecting Rio Arriba County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Chama below Chamita.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 6.0 feet, properties in the flood plain along the Rio
Chama and near the junction of the Rio Ojo Caliente will see water
in their yards. Impacts can include bank erosion and damage to
wells and septic tanks.  These impacts will increase in severity at
higher river levels.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:00 PM MDT Tuesday the stage was 6.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 6:00 PM MDT Tuesday was 6.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to oscillate around 6.4 to 6.5
feet through Wednesday.
- Flood stage is 6.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 6.4
feet on 07/21/2009.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday afternoon at noon MDT.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 27 at 6:54PM MDT until October 29 at 7:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Rio Puerco Near Bernardo affecting Socorro County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Puerco near Bernardo.

* WHEN...Until Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 23.0 feet, streets in the village of San Francisco
between interstate 25 and the Rio Grande just south of Bernardo are
being flooded. Water levels in the Lower Rio Puerco have not been
this high since July of 1944. The nearby railroad bridge may also
be flooded. Further rises will impact Interstate 25 traffic.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:00 PM MDT Tuesday the stage was 19.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
evening to a crest of 21.8 feet Wednesday morning. It will then
fall below flood stage Thursday.
- Flood stage is 19.5 feet.
- Flood History...No available flood history.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 27 at 8:52PM MDT until October 29 at 2:00AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Colorado...

Purgatoire River Near Las Animas affecting Bent County.

For the Purgatoire River...including Las Animas...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...High flow is traveling down the Upper Purgatoire from recent
rains, and may lead to flooding near Las Animas.

* WHERE...Purgatoire River near Las Animas.

* WHEN...Until late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Minor Flood. Minor agricultural flooding
occurs into low lying areas along the river.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 PM MDT Tuesday the stage was 9.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:15 PM MDT Tuesday was 9.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 9.7 feet
tomorrow morning. It will then fall below flood stage early
tomorrow afternoon.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 9.8
feet on 06/06/1949.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday morning at 900 AM MDT.
